text: A.J. Brown's status remains uncertain heading into Sunday's road matchup against the Dolphins, with the Patriots receiver questionable after sitting out the final two practices due to ankle and knee issues—the knee ailment representing a new concern layered atop his previously injured ankle. Meanwhile, the Patriots' secondary appears to be in solid shape, with Mike Reiss reporting the starting secondary healthy for the Dolphins game, a potential advantage as Miami looks to build momentum against the defending AFC champion Patriots. On the bright side for New England's offense, quarterback Drake Maye has been leading the league in passing yards on scramble drills this season, a superpower the Patriots have been capitalizing on in creative ways. Head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the team's preparations in his Friday press conference, though the injury situation—particularly Brown's status and any involvement from running back TreVeyon Henderson, who is also questionable—will likely be a key storyline as kickoff approaches.
